properties.name: The read-back under a claim shows a dispute the owner keeps open on purpose, and which route the owner holds as the reading, when those govern the claim's steps
properties.source: @ajs, 2026-10-18: "Capture the shortcomings (gaps) from the trial" (cogito trial)
properties.statement:
When a Decision set to `contested` governs steps under a claim, reasoning_report on that claim lists it in contested_by_design. When that Decision names one route as the reading the design holds, the read-back marks that route as the held reading and the others as rivals, rather than three equal alternatives.
MEASURED by the observer in the cogito trial (2026-10-18): dec:which-reading-of-the-cogito was set `contested` by the owner's word, with the three reading steps GOVERNED_BY it. reasoning_report on req:i-exist still read contested_by_design: [], and the owner's choice of reading B changed nothing. Only the unscoped walk roots contested Decisions, and through a hub that walk runs on the hub's own design (see the hub requirement recorded the same day).

ALSO MEASURED 2026-10-19 (trolley trial): reasoning_report ON a contested dispute Decision returns the Decision alone ("unsupported"). It does not walk the rival positions it governs. So the read-back should work in both directions: from a claim to the dispute that governs its steps, and from a dispute Decision to its positions, each with what it rests on (the issue/positions read-back, idea (f) of the frameworks decision).
